newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil hold earlier levels.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil hold earlier levels.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were steady from earlier levels, but down on the day with many players away for the Christmas holidays, industry sources said.
"Most players have already left for the day for the Christmas but there was some trading this afternoon," one broker said.
January gas oil was last quoted at $31.75/$31.85 per barrel, down from Monday's $31.90/$32.05. January traded earlier Tuesday at $31.85 and $31.80 a barrel, brokers said.
Traders said the softer prices on the day were due mainly to the weaker overnight crude values and maintained that Asian fundamentals have not changed.

"China is still in the market for January gas oil," one trader said. Sources reported an 80,000-tonne MidEast cargo was earlier sold for arrival in south China and Hong Kong in January at a premium of about $1.30 to Singapore spot quotes.

February Brent crude closed down 27 cents to $23.19 a barrel on Monday and January gas oil futures on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) also closed weaker, losing $3.50 to close at $211.50 per tonne.
The market was stronger on Monday after India awarded 720,000 tonnes of high speed diesel for arrival in February against earlier expectations of between 500,000 to 700,000 tonnes.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade remained firm with new buying seen from Indonesia on top of recent purchases from North Asia for the winter.
January regrade was quoted at $1.55/$1.75 a barrel. It traded on Monday at $1.60, brokers said.
January fuel oil was quoted at $119.50/$121.00 per tonne, down from Monday's $119.75/$120.50.
